title: Multiplex chromogenic immunohistochemistry to stain and analyze paraffin tissue sections from the mouse or human
protocol: Load slides into a rack and place in de-waxing xylenes, 2 × 5 min.
Transfer slides to ethanol 99% solution for 3 min.
Block any endogenous peroxidase activity by placing slides into H2O2 Endogenous peroxidase blocking solution, 2 × 3 min.
Transfer samples to final ethanol 99% solution for 3 min.
Rinse in running water, 1 min.
Replace the lid on the pressure cooker but do not lock it.
Allow solution to warm until boiling (∼10 min).
Carefully lower rehydrated histological slides into the boiling solution.
Replace the lid and lock it.
Set pressure selector to the highest-pressure symbol.
Start timing for 10 min once red pressure indicator has risen and steam is escaping from the outlet valve.
Switch off the hotplate using the dial after 10 minutes.
Carefully remove the pressure cooker and transfer to a sink.
Lift the valve or push a button/turn a dial to release steam from the pressure cooker.
Allow tissue slides to cool down in running tap water for 5 min.
Remove the slides from the pressure cooker and place them in a slide jar with ddH2O.
Ensure the slides do not dry out while cooling.
Store slides in ddH2O or TBS-Tween 20 if longer storage is needed.
Change reagents inside staining jars once a week, especially the H2O2 endogenous peroxidase blocking solution.
Use ImmEdge Hydrophobic Barrier PAP Pen to draw a circle around the specimen on the slide.
Transfer the slides into TBST.
Incubate the sections with 1% BSA-TBS for 30 min at room temperature.
Add 100–300 μL of primary antibody, Anti-PD-L1 (1:200, 4.37 μm/mL), to antibody diluent and incubate for 40 min at room temperature.
Rinse with TBST for 2 × 5 min at room temperature.
Apply 100–300 μL of anti-rabbit secondary antibody polymer conjugated (ImmPRESS® Polymer Reagent) Ready to Use.
Incubate for 45 min at room temperature.
Rinse with TBST for 2 × 5 min at room temperature.
Prepare VIP substrate chromogen following the manufacturer’s instructions using PBS as diluent.
Apply Vector VIP HRP substrate chromogen for 10 min at room temperature.
Transfer slides to running tap water for 2 min at RT.
Avoid direct contact from running tap water, as it could displace the tissue attached to the glass slide.
Incubate the slides in Harris Hematoxylin for 3 min at room temperature.
Transfer slides to running tap water for 2 min at room temperature.
Dip quickly in Acid alcohol (1%) for 2–3 seconds at room temperature.
Transfer slides to running tap water for 2 min.
Incubate in Ammonia water solution (0.2%) for 3 min.
Rinse in tap water for 2 min.
Transfer slides to ethanol 99% solution for 3 × 3 min.
Transfer slides to Xylene for 2 × 3 min.
Mount the slides using DPX mounting media, adding the coverslip.
Let the slides dry out for 12–16 hours under the fume hood.
Place the slides in the scanning tray.
Perform single or batch scanning according to the number of slides.
Set the Region of scan and place crosses in the focus points.
Set 40× as resolution.
Pause point: If needed, store the slides and re-start Round 2 when desired.
Store mounted stained tissue slides at room temperature in an airtight container if they are kept dry for up to two years.
Place the slides from round 1 into Xylene jar for at least 12–24 hours.
Remove the coverslip carefully.
Re-start the process of rehydration and antigen retrieval as in “rehydration and antigen retrieval round 1” section.
Optimize the HIER duration if strong staining is observed in previous rounds depending on the antibodies used.
Use PAP pen to draw a circle around the specimen on the slide.
Transfer the slides into TSBT.
Incubate sections with Fab fragment anti-rabbit (1:50 diluted in TBS) for 30 minutes.
Incubate sections with primary antibody anti-CD206 (1:1000, 1 μm/mL) in antibody diluent for 40 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse sections with TBST buffer for 2 × 5 minutes.
Apply secondary antibody polymer conjugated ready to use and incubate for 45 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse sections with TBST for 2 × 5 minutes.
Prepare VIP substrate chromogen following manufacturer instructions.
Apply Vector VIP HRP substrate chromogen for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer slides to running tap water.
Counterstain tissue sections.
Clear and mount tissue sections.
Scan tissue sections using a scanner.
Align images of two consecutive staining procedures.
Create a digital multiplex image for quantification.
Open QuPath and create a new project.
Add images to the QuPath project.
Set image type as Brightfield (H-DAB).
Import images into the QuPath project.
Select multi-view in QuPath to align images.
Add column in multi-view mode for image alignment.
Select similar ROIs in both images and export to ImageJ.
Create Annotation in left image.
Copy Annotation (Ctrl+D) and Paste in the other slide (SHIFT+E).
Click ImageJ Icon>set resolution 1>OK.
Repeat the process for all the annotations and save them in TIFF in ImageJ.
Create a new TrakEM2 project in FIJI ImageJ.
Move the required images into the created folder.
Import the ROIs for alignment.
Drag the folder containing PD-L1 and CD206 images from the same region into the TrakEM2 plugin.
Set up the alignment tools within TrakEM2.
Right-click on the first image, select “Align”> “Align stack slices”, and use default Registration options (Rigid Registration).
Scroll the mouse to verify the automatic alignment between the images.
If images are not aligned automatically, perform manual supervised co-registration as needed.
Right-click on the aligned image, select “Export”> ”Make flat image…”, choose Type: “RGB Color”, Start: “1: z=0.0 [layer]”, and End: “2: z=1.0 [layer]”.
Click Best Quality and continue to export the merged images in Tiff format.
Scroll the mouse to verify that the two staining images are completely aligned.
Transform stack to flat images by going to “Image”> “Stacks”> “Stacks to Images”.
Name each registered image.
Go to “Image”> “Color”> “Color Deconvolution”.
Choose Vector: “H AEC” for PD-L1 and “H DAB” for CD206 in the window.
Discard Channel 3 stack images.
Repeat the process for Channel 1 and Channel 2 Stacks.
Rename one image for Channel 1 or nuclear staining to Nuclei.
Keep both images from Channel 2, rename them as PD-L1 and CD206.
Go to “Image”> “Color”> “Merge Channels…”
Select “CD206” Image in C1 (red).
Select “PD-L1” Image in C2 (green).
Select “Nuclei” Image in C3 (blue).
Create a pseudo-color composite image.
Go to “Image”> “Color”> “Channel Tool…”
Set Channel to “Color” mode.
For “Channel 1”, select color “Red” in the “More” settings.
Invert the LUT for “Channel 1” by selecting “Edit LUT” and “Invert….”
Repeat steps 3 and 4 for Channel 2 using color Green.
Repeat steps 3 and 4 for Channel 3 using color Blue.
Change “Color” mode to “Composite”.
Save the image in Tiff format.
Create a project on QuPath.
Import composite images from all cases.
Change image type to “Fluorescence”.
Assign colors manually for each channel when importing the composite image.
Click on brightness and contrast icon to add color for each channel.
Use Channel 1: Blue, Channel 2: Green, and Channel 3: Red in this example.
Create annotations in all cases.
Generate annotation in the region of interest before any segmentation or analysis.
Use "channel 2" (green, CD206) for detection channel.
Set up an appropriate threshold to calculate different intensities.
Use "Channel 3: Cell Mean" (red, PD-L1) for "score compartment".
Set threshold +1: 30.
Set threshold +2: 50.
Set threshold +3: 70.
Optimize the score compartment based on antigen subcellular localization.
Adapt intensity thresholds to specific staining conditions.
Use percentage of positivity instead of Histoscore by clicking “single threshold” if needed.
Calculate H-score combining the intensity of staining (graded as: 0, non-staining; 1, weak; 2, median; or 3, strong) and the percentage of positive cells.
Export "Annotation measurement" table for quantification purposes.
Plot H-score results using Box-plot graph.
Show median with center line in Boxplots.
Display interquartile range as box in Boxplots.
Indicate min-max values with whiskers in Boxplots.
Represent individual mice data points with circles.
Calculate p-values by ANOVA with Yekutieli correction.
Use automation and batch analysis scripts for color deconvolution in FIJI.
Perform image analysis using QuPath software.
Create macros in Fiji-ImageJ using the recording tool.
Select Plugins>Macros>Record in ImageJ.
Start recording a macro before performing color deconvolution.
Select the image of interest after starting macro recording.
Run “Color Deconvolution” with vectors set to [H AEC].
Use a control image as template for optimizing cell segmentation and intensity thresholds in QuPath.
Optimize settings based on the control image.
Go to “Workflow”>” Create Workflow” in QuPath.
Select desired commands such as “Set Image type”, “Select objects by class”, and “Positive Cell Detection”.
